items.title: Origin Energy investigating 'potential' customer data breach
items.description: Origin Energy says it does not believe customer credit card or bank details have been affected by a suspected data breach at the company.

items.title: Minister says Australian IS-linked 'Doctor Jihad' can 'rot' in Iraqi jail
items.description: Perth paediatrician Tareq Kamleh went to Syria to join the Islamic State group in 2015 and has, until now, been presumed dead.

items.title: Live: Rebel Wilson celebrates win in defamation legal battle
items.description: Hollywood actor Rebel Wilson successfully defends a defamation case brought against her by the star of her directorial debut.

items.title: Former Socceroos captain Paul Wade reveals probable CTE diagnosis
items.description: Paul Wade says he wants to share his experience to raise awareness about concussion, repeated head impacts and brain health across all levels of football.

items.title: Lewis breaks Australian 100m record, beats five-time Olympic champ
items.description: Torrie Lewis shows she is hitting her straps ahead of the Commonwealth Games by beating her own record mark during a meet in Slovakia.

items.title: Who are the Houthis? The 'merchant of chaos' threatening to widen the war
items.description: The Houthi rebels, described as one of Iran's "merchants of chaos", have threatened to widen the conflict in the Middle East by declaring a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia. Here's what could happen next.

items.title: Gates Foundation met with Epstein about 30 times, review finds
items.description: Bill Gates was aware of Jeffrey Epstein's 2008 sex offence conviction during their association, an external review of the Gates Foundation finds.

items.title: Jewish community group details 'unprecedented' security needs
items.description: Police engagement failed to engender a sense of safety in Melbourne's Jewish community in the face of rising "vitriol", the antisemitism royal commission has heard.

items.title: Unlawful excavation of river cliff disturbs Aboriginal ancestral remains
items.description: A cliff site in South Australia's Riverland, home to Aboriginal ancestral remains, has been excavated without authorisation.

items.title: 'We do not want to highlight this yet': AI data centre's FAQ slip-up
items.description: Data centre builder Firmus posted a statement, since removed, indicating its intention to get some of its cooling water from the state-owned irrigation system, adding "but we do not want to highlight this yet".

items.title: Judge says there's a 'real risk' to safety of Bondi Beach attack witnesses
items.description: Twenty witnesses in the Bondi Beach terror attack case have been granted anonymity, with a judge saying there is a "real risk" to their safety.

items.title: Atlassian marks milestone in $1.4b 'world's tallest hybrid timber' tower in Sydney
items.description: When construction finishes next year, the Sydney building will be the tallest hybrid structure in the world by 100 metres.

items.title: Boy charged with murdering mother, attempting to kill sister in Perth
items.description: A 16-year-old boy is charged with murdering his mother and attempting to kill his sister in Perth's south-east, as police say the girl is being treated in hospital for "very serious" stab wounds.

items.title: NT enacts 'significant overhaul' of child protection system
items.description: The Northern Territory parliament has passed changes to child protection laws, with the Country Liberal Party describing its amendments as "the most significant overhaul of the Territory's child protection system in a generation".

items.title: As The Odyssey smashes box office records, one name is drawing people in
items.description: The Odyssey's director Sir Christopher Nolan has a stellar catalogue. Interstellar, even. But as his new film smashes box office records, is it safe to crown him the new king of Hollywood?

items.title: New Ozploitation horror is like Puberty Blues from hell
items.description: After spending years in special effects and make-up, filmmaker Mia'Kate Russell's ocker nightmare Penny Lane Is Dead has made it to the silver screen.

items.title: 'I just laid in his cot and cried': Mothers on child loss
items.description: Women who have lost children talk about continuing in the wake of such grief, and how people stepped up, or stepped away.

items.title: Cameron McEvoy has lived a life between trips to Glasgow
items.description: As one of just two Australian swimmers returning to Glasgow for a second Commonwealth Games, Cameron McEvoy is taking time to appreciate how much has happened to him in the past 12 years.

items.title: Fox sisters combine in 'dream team' for gold medals at World Championships
items.description: Noemie Fox labels her partnership with older sister Jess a "dream team" after the pair combined for another set of gold medals at the IFC Canoe Slalom World Championships in Oklahoma.

items.title: States can use their own emergency warnings when AusAlert goes live
items.description: State and territory representatives had voiced significant concerns about the rollout of the national emergency warning system in a meeting with the minister Kristy McBain.

items.title: Albanese's career mirrors Howard's in two important ways
items.description: Anthony Albanese has been in near-fatal vehicle accidents not once, but three times. Politically, his is also a story of survival against the odds.

items.title: Woman's family wrongly told she was dead in hospital identity error
items.description: A Melbourne hospital apologises after mixing up the medical data of two people, resulting in one of them being wrongly declared dead by police.

items.title: How school is different for Jewish Australian kids
items.description: The Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion hears from Jewish school leaders about how they need to implement extraordinary and expensive security measures.

items.title: Godzilla actor killed in car crash
items.description: US investigators say speed was a likely factor in the crash that killed actor Kaylee Hottle, 18.

items.title: AI companies 'stole' Australian culture, news bosses say
items.description: The heads of the ABC, SBS, Nine and News Corp say AI companies should strike licensing deals rather than freely train on Australian news, warning journalism is a public good that must be protected.
